summary_en: This work presents an end-to-end virtual imaging framework for three-dimensional quantitative optoacoustic tomography of the breast. It extends stochastic numerical breast phantoms with multiple skin tones and benign and malignant lesions, simulates optical fluence and initial-pressure generation, and models transducer spatial and acousto-electric responses to generate realistic measurement data. A system-design case study and the release of 1,020 phantoms make it directly useful for reconstruction-method development and objective optoacoustic imager evaluation.
